definitions.explanation: Being so absorbed in an activity or emotion that one forgets oneself. Most commonly seen in the set phrase {無我夢中|むがむちゅう}.
The Buddhist doctrine that there is no permanent, independent self — one of the three marks of existence. Used in Buddhist and philosophical contexts.

examples.japanese: {無我夢中|むがむちゅう}で{走|はし}った。
examples.english: I ran in a self-forgetful frenzy.

examples.japanese: {演奏|えんそう}{中|ちゅう}は{無我|むが}になって{時間|じかん}を{忘|わす}れていた。
examples.english: While performing, I lost myself and forgot the time.

examples.japanese: {仏教|ぶっきょう}の{無我|むが}の{思想|しそう}。
{釈迦|しゃか}は{無我|むが}を{説|と}いた。
examples.english: Shakyamuni taught the doctrine of no-self.

examples.japanese: {無我|むが}の{教|おし}えは{執着|しゅうちゃく}からの{解放|かいほう}を{目指|めざ}す{考|かんが}え{方|かた}だ。
examples.english: The teaching of no-self aims at liberation from attachment.

notes:
Composed of {無|む} (without) + {我|が} (self, ego). In daily Japanese the everyday sense (self-forgetful absorption) is far more common than the Buddhist doctrinal sense.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {無我夢中|むがむちゅう}: in a self-forgetful frenzy
- {無我|むが}の{境地|きょうち}: a state of selflessness
- {無我|むが}になる: to lose oneself (in something)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {夢中|むちゅう}: absorbed; engrossed — everyday word for being absorbed in something
- {無心|むしん}: free of distractions; innocent — emphasizes a mind clear of thought
- {忘我|ぼうが}: self-forgetfulness; ecstasy — literary; emphasizes losing oneself in emotion
